module_title: Fundamental Duties - The 11th Duty, MCQs Traps, and Rejected Recommendations
introduction: At this level, we focus on the specific duties listed in Article 51A, the crucial addition of the 11th duty regarding education, and the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee that the government chose NOT to accept.

core_concepts.title: The 11th Fundamental Duty
core_concepts.description: Added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002. It states: 'It is the duty of every citizen who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of 6 and 14 years.'

core_concepts.title: Scope of Duties
core_concepts.description: Fundamental Duties are confined ONLY to citizens. Unlike some Fundamental Rights (like Art 14 or 21) which extend to foreigners, duties do not apply to non-citizens.

core_concepts.title: Rejected Recommendations
core_concepts.description: The Swaran Singh Committee suggested 8 duties, but 10 were added. Congress rejected some of its bold suggestions: 1) Imposing a penalty/punishment for non-compliance of duties, 2) Duty to pay taxes.

core_concepts.title: Key Civic and Moral Duties
core_concepts.description: Civic duties include respecting the Constitution, National Flag, and National Anthem. Moral duties include cherishing the noble ideals of the freedom struggle and promoting harmony.

important_entities.name: Atal Bihari Vajpayee Government
important_entities.significance: Under his tenure in 2002, the 11th duty regarding children's education was added, aligning with the insertion of Article 21A (Right to Education).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In MCQs, you will often be asked to identify which is NOT a fundamental duty. 'Paying taxes', 'Voting in elections', and 'Family planning' are NOT Fundamental Duties, even though they are good civic practices.
Article 51A(a) mentions respecting the National Flag and the National Anthem. It does NOT explicitly mention the National Song (Vande Mataram).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A: Abide by the constitution; B: Cherish noble ideals of freedom struggle; C: Uphold sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize the exact phrasing of the 11th duty and the amendment that added it (86th CAA, 2002).
Expect 'Odd One Out' questions where three options are actual duties, and the fourth is 'To cast vote' or 'To pay taxes'.
